name: Chase Tower block, N Central Ave
why_chosen: The tallest building in Arizona, in the deepest street canyon Phoenix has. Low sky-view factor clips the afternoon peak and then suppresses radiative cooling after sunset. Night shift, because downtown utility and street work is done at night. THIS IS THE DEMO'S LEAD SITE — a crew working 21:00 to 05:30 whose entire risk window is invisible to a forecast that reports a daytime maximum.

name: Superior Court complex, W Jefferson St

It tests something narrower and still worth knowing: whether the API's 20 m grid resolves intra-district variation at all, or whether both downtown sites return the same numbers. If they are identical, the site-level claim weakens everywhere.

name: Loop 202 South Mountain corridor paving
why_chosen: Freeway corridor on the desert fringe in Ahwatukee, night paving crew of 18 — the largest crew on the roster. The interesting case: an open desert-edge site should cool fast after dark, so this crew may be the SAFEST on the roster despite sitting at one of the highest daytime peaks. If the tool says so it is arguing against the intuition that a hot site means a hot shift, which is the entire point of measuring duration inside the shift window instead of reporting a maximum.

Evaporative damping with almost no canopy, which separates the two cooling mechanisms: if this tracks Encanto Park the driver is evaporation, if it tracks the asphalt sites the driver was shade all along.
